repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CXHfRgU81naozMNwDa

Decision analysis · 2026-11-26T04:41Z · decision thread for zone o5-P (card thread report on PR #37428, head 93cc4af1)

## 维护者速读

- 问题：开发者用命令行新建项目拿到的空白模板，要改成和起步应用一模一样的公司、联系人。可是脚手架那道检查是拿 npm 上已发布的 18.6.0 去验新模板的，而起步应用用了三种 11 月 18 日之后才加的写法（对象颜色、分组里直接列字段、相关列表带列），所以这个改动过不了检查，停在草稿。外面的开发者不受影响：不管怎么选，新模板都要到 19 发出来才到他们手里。
- 选项：A 模板不动，改动先停着，等第一个 19 预发布版发出后检查自己变绿，不用新 PR；B 把模板改回 18.6 认识的旧写法，现在能合，发版后再改回来，前后两个 PR，其间模板和起步应用不一样；C 让检查去装每晚快照，一个受管 PR，但 19 预发布期间快照通道是停的，只救得了这一次；D 让这道检查改用本仓库当场打出来的包（另一条脚手架检查已经这样做），一个受管 PR，以后模板跟着主干走，不再被旧版本卡住。
- 推荐 A 加 D：这次先等，不为迁就旧版本把模板写走样；同时立卡把检查改成验「将要一起发出去的那一套」，因为 19 这条线上每个改写法的破坏性改动都会再撞一次。
- 不定会怎样：这个改动一直停着；19 这条线上下一个改到模板所用写法的破坏性改动，会同样卡住。

## Background

Card #36945 (epic #36941, maintainer-directed) swaps the blank template's sample `note` object for the Starter app's companies and contacts, "identical to the starter app's definitions", held by a parity pin so the two never drift. Draft PR #37428 does that. Its only red beyond a separately named two-line gap is the job `Scaffold with repo dist` in `.github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml`: it builds the scaffolder from the PR, scaffolds a project, then installs that project's `@objectstack/*` dependencies from the npm registry at the repo version and runs validate, build, test, boot and a Docker run.

The repo version is 18.6.0 and so is npm `latest` (published 2026-11-18). Since then about 930 changesets have landed unreleased, and on 2026-11-25 the v19 line opened (PR #37230): Changesets is in pre mode, every release from here is a `19.0.0-next.N` prerelease on the `next` dist-tag, and `latest` stays on 18.x until 19.0 GA. The Starter's source uses three shapes that landed after 18.6.0, so the published 18.6.0 refuses the template the PR ships. The job is testing the template of the next release against the framework of the last one, a pairing no user installs: `create-objectstack` and `@objectstack/spec` are in one `fixed` group and always publish together.

## Governing text

- Card #36945, What 1 and 2: the template ships companies and contacts "as source, identical to the starter app's definitions", with "one source of truth ... so the two never drift". B contradicts this ruled scope.
- `.github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml` header: the gate exists because "the bundled template drifted from the published framework" and "nothing ever exercised the published package end-to-end"; job 1 "runs the generated project against the registry", job 2 (nightly) uses the published `create-objectstack@latest`. — `sed -n 3,18p .github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml`
- Same file, install step: the only window it knows is "right after a version bump lands but before the release publishes", handled by a fallback that rewrites the ranges to `latest` and re-stamps `engines.protocol`. A long unreleased window with the version already published is not a case it names. — `sed -n 69,131p .github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml`
- Same file: moving that fallback into the shipped scaffolder was declined at triage on 2026-08-17 (#9149); reopening needs a decision card. D does not reopen it: D changes what the CI job installs, not what a user's scaffolder does. — `sed -n 311,325p .github/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml`
- `scripts/create-scaffold-smoke.sh` (maintainer ruling on #14824, the sibling scaffolder `os create`): "a literal registry install could only ever test the PREVIOUS release, i.e. not the change under review. `pnpm pack` applies the same manifest rewrites as `pnpm publish`, so a tarball is what npm would hand a downstream installer." This is the in-repo precedent for D. — `sed -n 19,32p scripts/create-scaffold-smoke.sh`
- ADR-0125, amendment of 2026-11-05: the `next` snapshot lane refuses "while `.changeset/pre.json` says `mode: pre`" because the major's cycle owns the channel. C depends on that lane. — `grep -n "Not during a major" docs/adr/0125-release-approval-gate-replaces-the-typed-version.md`
- `.changeset/37223-v19-line-opens.md`: "Every release from here is a `19.0.0-next.N` prerelease on the npm dist-tag `next`, until 19.0 GA"; a plain install "stays on 18.x until 19.0 GA".
- pm-dispatch state model: a card waiting on a platform release is `pm:on-hold` with a machine-readable `Restart-when:` naming the install-surface criterion; a red check may be queued only when the workflow source itself says it is red by design, which this one does not.
- pm-dispatch `references/decision-analysis.md`, app-repo order: when the blocker is the platform not having shipped, recommend waiting, never a shape workaround. Written for app repos; read here by analogy only.

## Protocol

No spec change under any option. `Metadata-protocol: none`. A and D leave the template in the shapes the Starter and the skills teach; B would publish the older spelling in the template.

## Premises (each with a re-check)

1. npm `latest` is 18.6.0; `next` is `0.0.0-next-20261125013212`. — `npm view @objectstack/spec dist-tags --json`
2. Repo version 18.6.0, pre mode with tag `next`, 931 pending changesets at f9dd0331. — `node -p "require('./packages/spec/package.json').version"; cat .changeset/pre.json; ls .changeset/*.md | grep -vi readme | wc -l`
3. The Starter uses object `color`, `fieldGroups[].fields` and object-form `relatedLists`. — `grep -n "color: '\|fieldGroups\|relatedLists" -A3 examples/app-starter/src/objects/company.object.ts`
4. Published 18.6.0 has none of the three; the last snapshot has all three. Read statically from the two published tarballs (marker strings `OBJECT_COLOR`, `listed members`, `this relatedLists entry`: 0/0/0 files in 18.6.0, 12/6/2 in the snapshot). The card thread measured the behaviour on a real registry install: validate fails on `color`, and passes with the three stripped. — `npm pack @objectstack/spec@18.6.0` and `@0.0.0-next-20261125013212`, then `grep -rlF` over `package/dist`
5. The v19 line opened with PR #37230, merged 2026-11-25T12:51Z; the last snapshot was published 2026-11-25T02:01Z, before it. No snapshot can be cut until 19.0 GA (premise from ADR-0125 above). — `npm view @objectstack/spec time --json | tail -4`
6. The Version Packages PR #35129 still renders 18.7.0 (last refreshed 2026-11-25T12:13Z). The two bookkeeping runs since the line opened failed at "Validate the post-version tree" (runs 45671808843 and 45727328727). PR #37314 (PROTOCOL_VERSION 18 to 19) is open; `release.yml` refuses a version commit that moves `protocol-version.ts`, so it reads as the prerequisite. The failing step's error line was not read. — `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pulls/35129`, `GET .../actions/workflows/release.yml/runs?event=schedule`
7. `scaffold-e2e.yml` is path-filtered, has no `merge_group` trigger and is not a required context. — `grep -n -i scaffold scripts/check-required-contexts.mjs` (0 hits); `grep -n "advisory in the same way" .github/workflows/os-create-smoke.yml`
8. Load on the job: 29 pull-request runs since 2026-11-10 outside the release branch (about 1.8 a day), 25 green, median 3 min 45 s. The packed-tarball sibling `os-create-smoke.yml` took 10 min on its last pull-request run (2026-11-19) and 4 to 15 min nightly. — `GET .../actions/workflows/scaffold-e2e.yml/runs?event=pull_request&per_page=100`, same for `os-create-smoke.yml`
9. Inside the monorepo the new template already passes against the workspace's own packages (PR #37428 body: validate, lint, typecheck, `starter.test.ts` 3/3). The registry job is the only check that runs it outside the monorepo, and it runs it against 18.6.0.

## The question in one sentence

A change that makes the new-project template match the Starter app cannot land, because the check that guards the template tests it against the last published release instead of the code it will ship with.

## Options × real cost × workload

| | What | What people see | Workload |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Keep the Starter-identical source. Hold the PR until npm carries a version that satisfies the template's pin and accepts the three shapes, which is the first `19.0.0-next.N` cut. The job then goes green with no change. | Developers: nothing changes under any option until 19 ships. Fleet: the card waits on a chain that is the maintainer's own (PR #37314, then the Version Packages PR renders 19.0.0-next.0, then merge and release approval). The PR lands after that cut, so `@next` users get the template one prerelease later. The same stall returns for every later change that moves the template to a shape newer than the last cut. | 0 PRs. Card to `pm:on-hold` with `Restart-when:`. |
| B | Write the template in shapes 18.6.0 accepts (per-field `group`, no object `color`, string `relatedLists`), with a named delta list in the parity pin, removed after the release. | The template lands now, in a spelling the Starter and the skills no longer teach, and stays that way until someone removes the delta. If major 19 retires an old spelling first, the template is broken against main instead. | 2 PRs (delta now, removal later). About 150 lines by the card thread's estimate; no precedent. |
| C | Governed change to `scaffold-e2e.yml`: when the repo holds unreleased changesets, install the `next` dist-tag instead of the pinned version. | Greens this PR today, because the last snapshot happens to predate the v19 line and already carries the three shapes. Dead from then on: no snapshot is cut in pre mode, and once 19.0.0-next.0 exists the pin resolves it natively. After 19 GA it narrows the gap to the snapshot cadence (3 published in the last 11 days, each needing an approval). | Tier H, 1 PR, no precedent. Also needs the protocol re-stamp reworked: a snapshot is versioned 0.0.0, and the existing re-stamp reads the installed spec's major (read from the workflow, not run). |
| D | Governed change to `scaffold-e2e.yml`, filed as its own card: `Scaffold with repo dist` installs the generated project from this checkout's packed tarballs through the project's own overrides, the way `os-create-smoke.yml` does, and the `latest` fallback and protocol re-stamp (about 60 lines) go. The nightly `Registry canary` keeps exercising the published scaffolder against the real registry. | A red on that job then means one thing: the template does not work with the code it ships with. Template changes stop depending on the release calendar, in either direction: a new shape is testable the day it merges, and a retired shape is caught on the retiring PR instead of on the canary after publish. The job gets slower, about 4 min to about 10 min, on about 2 PRs a day. | Tier H, domain:devx, 1 PR, size M to L. Precedent: PR #15535 (the #14824 gate, +1166/−141 over 13 files; workflow +123, script +257). |

Business translation. A: do not reprint the brochure in last season's wording; wait for the season to open. B: reprint it in last season's wording so the proof-reader passes it, and reprint again next month. C: ask the proof-reader to use a draft that stops being issued during the season. D: have the proof-reader check the brochure against this season's catalogue, the one it will be mailed with.

## Four axes (business stance)

- **Long-term fit (①)** — End state two years out: the pull-request gate for the scaffolder answers "does what we are about to publish work together", from packed bits outside the monorepo; the nightly canary answers "does what we already published still work". That is two questions with one job each, and it is how the mainstream scaffolders are tested: Nx and the Angular CLI publish the workspace to a local registry and scaffold against it, and Next.js tests `create-next-app` against a tarball of the repo's own `next`. The repo already chose this for `os create` (#14824). A is the honest reading of the card's ruled scope for this PR; D removes the cause. B bends the product (the template every new project and every AI author starts from) to satisfy a test's stale assumption. C adds a branch to the workaround the job already carries and leaves the question it asks unchanged.
- **Real business need (②)** — Measured pull: one PR today (#37428, p1, maintainer-directed epic). Predicted pull with a named card: the v19 line is a run of breaking changes, and any one that touches a shape the template uses must change the template in the same PR and will be refused by the last cut in the same way. The zone named the #37112 family (major 19 view and form shapes) as a candidate; whether it touches a shape the template uses was not verified here. No developer outside is waiting on any option: the template reaches `latest` users at 19.0 GA whichever is chosen, so B's only gain is an earlier merge inside the repo.
- **AI-error-proofing (③)** — The blank template is what an AI author copies from.
